finding: NAION found without being told to look for it
detail: Optic ischaemic neuropathy on semaglutide: PRR 100.0 on 625 cases, and it signals on dulaglutide and tirzepatide too. The EMA PRAC concluded NAION was a very rare side effect of semaglutide in June 2025 - inside this data window. The reference set is time-indexed for exactly this: the method is not being scored against a label it could have memorised.

finding: Suicidality: the primary term stays quiet, two rarer terms do not
detail: Suicidal ideation on semaglutide sits at PRR 1.43 on 176 cases - below the Evans threshold, agreeing with EMA PRAC (Apr 2024) and FDA (Jan 2026), both of which found no causal link. But Depression suicidal (PRR 2.74) and Self-injurious ideation (PRR 2.02) do clear Evans on counts in the teens, so the group verdict reads REPLICATED. That is what Evans criteria do on rare terms, and the scorecard reports it as a false positive rather than hiding it.

finding: A labelled risk that reports below background on every molecule
detail: Acute kidney injury is a Warning and Precaution on all four molecules and comes back under PRR 1 on all four - semaglutide at PRR 0.54 on 162 cases, 10 of 12 reference pairs below background. The mechanism is real; what fails is the comparator. This class draws an enormous volume of non-serious consumer reports, and disproportionality cannot see a risk that is common in the denominator too. Gate 3 was set at 6 of 8 so an honest negative need not be argued away.

finding: Dulaglutide and gastroparesis: a reporting artefact, not a risk ranking
detail: The gastroparesis group on dulaglutide runs at PRR 81 on 974 cases - 24.2% of every dulaglutide case in the cohort, against 5.9% of semaglutide's. A share that size on one molecule for one syndrome is not how spontaneous reporting distributes, and dulaglutide is the molecule named in US gastroparesis litigation running across this window. The PRR is correct and reading it as a risk ranking against the other three would be wrong. Confirming the mechanism needs reporter occupation, which this pipeline does not carry through to the GLP-1 cohort - it is a stated limitation, not a finding.

finding: Injection-site burden separates the two newer molecules
detail: Tirzepatide: PRR 3.8 on 10,111 cases, 14.4% of its cohort. Semaglutide: PRR 1.00 on 1,518 cases, 4.3% - sitting exactly on the FAERS background, so injection-site reactions are no more likely to be reported for semaglutide than for an average drug. Same class, same route, one measured difference. Device, formulation and injection-frequency differences are all candidates, and this data cannot separate them.

finding: Class effects are separable from molecule-specific ones
detail: 27 clinical events signal on all four molecules (23 individual PTs and 4 grouped signals), which is the strongest evidence available here for a class effect rather than a property of one product. Running four molecules against a common comparator instead of one is what makes that distinction possible at all, and it is also what isolates findings 4 and 5.
